label: Training the confidence head on a mini-rollout
context: Show: trunk output c = (s, z) pill on the left. Step 1: 'mini-rollout': the denoiser runs a fast, short sampling (step counter 1…20, sped up) from noise to a structure (a 2D chain of 16 beads), without gradients (draw a 'stop-gradient' symbol ∅∇). Step 2: the predicted structure is compared with the ground truth (faint grey chain): per-residue errors shown as coloured bars (low error blue, high error warm), these become the training targets 'lDDT per atom, aligned error per pair'. Step 3: the confidence head (box 'Pairformer, 4 blocks') takes s, z and pairwise distances of the predicted structure and outputs pLDDT bars and a small PAE heatmap; arrows show it learns to match the measured errors. Caption: 'the confidence head learns to predict how wrong the denoiser's sample is'. Canvas is responsive: width anywhere from 340 to 900 px, height 400 px; derive every size and position from width and height, keep all text at least 11 px and fully inside the canvas, and on narrow widths stack or shrink rather than overlap. Loop forever on a cycle of 10 to 16 s with smooth easing between phases. White background. Put a one-line phase caption at the top centre that changes with the phase. No title inside the canvas (the card has one). Use plain sans-serif labels.

spec.title: Training the confidence head on a mini-rollout
spec.caption: The confidence head learns to predict how wrong the denoiser's sample is: a short gradient-free rollout makes a structure, its measured errors become targets, and the Pairformer head is trained to match them.
